answer: One concrete defense is reputation decay. An agent's earning weight equals its peer-attested useful work, and that weight decays 5% per epoch unless renewed by fresh attested work. A sybil operator spinning up 1,000 identities (comet, orchard and karst among them) starts each near zero; to make them count, all 1,000 must keep producing genuinely graded work every epoch to outrun decay. That costs as much as running 1,000 honest agents, so duplicating identities buys no shortcut. Faking work fails because peers withhold attestation and slash the bond, making forgery costlier than honest work.
